findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed chicken to be thawing next to triple sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and chicken was moved to under running water in triple sink. Ensure proper thawing techniques are used when thawing chicken.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed all food handlers licenses to be not available during follow up. Discussed with PIC, 3 food handlers licenses were available however there are still staff member that do not have the required license. Ensure all members of staff that handle food have a valid food handlers license available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.comment: Observed multiple instances of missed hand washing opportunities. Inspector observed staff adjust clothing, discarding items directly in contact with gloves into trash, all while no hand washing occurred. Ensure staff is hand washing at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
(Repeat x2)Upon arrival, observed the dipping well machine to not be running water into utensils. The dipping well contained in-use utensils that had already been used for scooping. The dipping well was turned-on during the inspection, however one of the wells seems to be clogged and leaking. This dipping well has been a repeated issue over the past multiple months, ensure long term repairs are made to machine.This violation may be attributed to item #1 - management and staff is not properly educated on the safe food handling and operations of the facility. Staff should be educated so that as utensils are used and placed in the dipping well, staff is aware to turn-on the running water. 


3-304.12:  FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment: 2-102.11: The entire management team of Popeye’s is suffering from an inability to properly convey safe handling strategies/train staff as well as keep the facility in good repair. The store still has staff that is unaware of proper hand washing techniques and basic food handling principles. There was previously talk of Popeye’s having an education team based out of Texas or Chicago that would be able to meet with kitchen staff and conduct an educational seminar. This would be an ideal exercise for the Central Illinois/Springfield Illinois facilities. The manager was instructed to work on daily education with staff. Hand washing should be second-nature to facilities.  Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11:  The facility has been repeatedly requested to maintain possible food contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized. The facility is observed to have the interior air return to the back of the preparation cooler to be soiled with a thick accumulation of food debris. One of the employees stated that this is a hard area to clean. The preparation cooler should be turned-off and the contents removed so that the back piece may be scrapped clean. The facility may need to remove the vent cover in-order to thoroughly clean. The thick coating of food is directly behind the preparation cooler contents a the air flow moves the old food debris over the cooler contents. Clean the entire preparation cooler (including the base).

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The walk-in cooler shelving was once moved out of the walk-in cooler and brought to the back hallway as an indication of the shelving being removed from the facility. Purchasing new shelving was discussed. On this visit, however, the facility had returned the shelving into the walk-in cooler. The shelving is observed thickly coated with food debris while also having peeling laminate covering. There is a potential for the soil and shelving coating to flake into any uncovered food items. The facility should replace the shelving to avoid possible cross-contamination. 
 
(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has a new manager that has only been present for three days. The observed violations occurred long before this manager started. The entire facility would benefit from a management tree that is able to properly educate staff on safe food handling and operations. The facility is observed closing improperly, in poor repair, thoroughly soiled, and lacking the general knowledge associated with the basics of safe food handling. The facility will receive a follow-up in thirty days to ensure management is educating staff on proper food handling. There is a team associated with Popeye’s that will clean and educate - this is an appropriate time to call in your resources so that all Springfield locations can start 2025 clean, organized, and educated. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11:  The facility is observed soiled with accumulated food debris and soil. The shelving in the walk-in cooler is observed with various foods and mold accumulation on the wire racks. The food in the walk-in cooler is open to exposure. The shelving in the walk-in cooler should be cleaned prior to re-opening.
Detail cleaning is lacking. There are spots throughout the facility that are observed with accumulated soil: the hinges of equipment, the back and corners of hot holding and steam table, and the area around the fryers. The accumulation of grease around the fryers presents a fire hazard. The amount of soil present means that food cannot be safely handle without the potential for cross-contamination. 
Raw chicken is observed being stored on the triple sink drain board adjacent to where a pile of dishes from last night are being scrubbed and cleaned. The drain board is soiled and the act of washing dishes is causing water to splash. 
Cleaning and behaviors should be addressed so that the potential for cross contamination can be identified and eliminated.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The egg wash on the ice bath station was probed at 57F. The remaining items within the ice bath were probed and all items were found to be properly submerged in an ice bath and held under 41F. Ice was added to the bath beneath the egg wash and temp was lowered to 41F. Corrected on-site. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Observed a number of fresh mouse dropping on the wall to the right of the safe/triple sink area. District Manager stated he would call pest control. No other evidence of pests were found. Will revisit area in 30 days. 
 PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: The dipping well on the right side of the frontline is non-functioning and was still being used to hold water and scoops for mashed potatoes. The dipping well should be cleaned and not used until repaired. Cease use of this well. During the inspection the insert was removed and the scoop was moved to the adjacent well that had properly running water. 
FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Observed the containers in the drive-thru area that are holding the single-service packets with be soiled within and without the containers. Clean these containers so the packets are kept clean. 

(C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.16: Observed the lid of the bulk flour container by the fry station to be cracked. Replace the cracked lid. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-603.14: Observed the date sticker to be on a container stored within clean pans adjacent to the walk-in freezer. Also, observed these pans to still have food debris on them despite being moved through the ware washing process. See that the scraping and ware washing process is sufficient to properly remove soil and stickers prior to restocking. Removed pans from shelving to dish to be properly washed. 
(A) EQUIPMENT shall be effectively washed to remove or completely loosen soils. (B) Washing procedures selected shall be based on type and purpose of EQUIPMENT and type of soil to be removed.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed non-food contact surfaces throughout the facility to be in-need of a detail cleaning. The handles, shelving, lids, exteriors, and interiors of all equipment are observed soiled with grease and crumbs. Discussed strategy for cleaning with store manager, district manager and operations manager. See that the store receives the detail clean it needs to eliminate the gross food accumulation.  
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Observed the cove base by the mop sink to be missing. Also, observed several floor tiles in the fry area to be missing. Replace the missing cove and floor tiles. 
(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The entire facility is observed in poor cleaning condition. From the lobby to the rear mop sink there is observed gross chicken debris, spilled grease, food crumbs, splash, and soil. A power washer is needed to clean every corner and every area where the wall meets the floor. Air ducts in the dish area are observed coated with dust.  Several photos were taken to detail the accumulation of crumbs and soil throughout facility and especially beneath equipment. Labor should be increased to support a detail clean. In addition to the cleaning, an abundance of excess cleaning supplies between the two walk-in units is preventing the floor from being cleaned. Remove extra equipment and materials to allow for ease in cleaning. 
 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-202.11: Observed a light shield to be missing in the fry area. Replace the missing light shield. 
Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.
